questions.questionText:
A teacher asks a student to measure the volume of a pencil sharpener.
Which piece of apparatus would not be useful?

options.text: beaker
displacement can
balance
measuring cylinder

questions.questionText:
A student uses a force meter to measure the weights and a balance to measure the masses of
four different objects.
He puts his measurements in a table.
Which row is correctly recorded?
mass weight

options.text: 1kg 10N
5g 50N
20kg 2N

questions.questionText:
Which substance in the table has the lowest density?
substance mass/g volume/cm3

options.text: nylon 1.2 1.0
cotton 1.5 1.0
olive oil 1.8 2.0
water 2.0 2.0

questions.questionText:
A spacecraft is travelling in space with no resultant force and no resultant moment acting on it.
Which statement about the spacecraft is correct?

options.text: Its direction is changing.
It is in equilibrium.
Its speed is decreasing.
Its speed is increasing.

questions.questionText:
Electrical energy may be obtained from nuclear fission.
In which order is the energy transferred in this process?

options.text: nuclear fuel  generator  reactor and boiler  turbines
nuclear fuel  generator  turbines  reactor and boiler
nuclear fuel  reactor and boiler  generator  turbines
nuclear fuel  reactor and boiler  turbines  generator

questions.questionText:
A person lifts a book from floor level to a shelf. It falls to the floor and a second person lifts it back
up to the shelf.
Which statement must be correct?

options.text: The second person does the same work on the book as the first person.
The second person takes the same time as the first person.
The second person develops the same power as the first person.
The second person does the same work on the book as the first person, develops the same power and takes the same time.

questions.questionText:
A liquid is evaporating. The liquid is not boiling.
Which statement about the liquid is correct at an instant in time?

options.text: Any molecule can escape, and from any part of the liquid.
Any molecule can escape, but only from the liquid’s surface.
Only molecules with enough energy can escape, and only from the liquid’s surface.
Only molecules with enough energy can escape, but from any part of the liquid.

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows a sealed gas cylinder with a movable piston.
movable
piston
gas
The piston is moved slowly downwards and there is no change in temperature of the gas.
What happens to the average distance between the gas molecules and to the pressure of the
gas?
average distance
pressure of gas
between gas
in cylinder
molecules

options.text: decreases decreases
decreases increases
increases decreases
increases increases

questions.questionText:
A long, thin bar of copper is heated gently and evenly along its length.
copper bar
heat
What happens to the bar?

options.text: It becomes less heavy.
It becomes longer.
It becomes shorter.
It bends at the ends.

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows a pan used for cooking food.
handle of pan
base of pan
Which row is correct for the materials used to make the base and the handle of the pan?
base of pan handle of pan

options.text: good thermal conductor good thermal conductor
good thermal conductor poor thermal conductor
poor thermal conductor good thermal conductor
poor thermal conductor poor thermal conductor

questions.questionText:
The diagrams show two patterns produced by water waves.
diagram 1 diagram 2
barrier
barrier
Which two effects are shown in the diagrams?
diagram 1 diagram 2

options.text: reflection diffraction
reflection refraction
refraction diffraction
refraction reflection

questions.questionText:
Which row correctly defines the frequency and the speed of a wave?
frequency speed

options.text: number of waves distance travelled per unit time
number of waves time taken for one complete wave to pass a point
number of waves distance travelled passing per unit time per unit time
number of waves time taken for one complete passing per unit time wave to pass a point

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows a ray of light in air incident on a glass block. Some of the light is refracted
and some of the light is reflected. Two angles, p and q, are marked on the diagram.
ray of
light
air
glass
Which row gives the angle of incidence and states whether total internal reflection occurs?
angle of total internal
incidence reflection

options.text: p no
p yes
q no
q yes

questions.questionText:
Visible light, X-rays and microwaves are all components of the electromagnetic spectrum.
Which statement about the waves is correct?

options.text: In a vacuum, microwaves travel faster than visible light and have a shorter wavelength.
In a vacuum, microwaves travel at the same speed as visible light and have a shorter wavelength.
In a vacuum, X-rays travel faster than visible light and have a shorter wavelength.
In a vacuum, X-rays travel at the same speed as visible light and have a shorter wavelength.

questions.questionText: What can transmit some types of transverse waves but not longitudinal waves?

options.text: air
a steel bar
a vacuum
sea water

questions.questionText: What is ultrasound?

options.text: sound waves that are so loud that they damage human hearing
sound waves that are too high-pitched for humans to hear
sound waves that are too low-pitched for humans to hear
sound waves that are too quiet for humans to hear

questions.questionText: What would be the least successful method of magnetising a steel bar?

options.text: Insert the bar in a coil with a large direct current (d.c.).
Place the bar at right angles to a weak magnetic field and hit it with a hammer.
Place the bar parallel to a strong magnetic field, heat it and let it cool.
Stroke the bar with a magnet.

questions.questionText:
An electric current in a copper wire is due to the flow of charge.
Which particles are moving along the wire?

options.text: -particles
copper nuclei
electrons
protons

questions.questionText:
Which row correctly shows a conductor and an insulator?
conductor insulator

options.text: rubber plastic
iron nylon
air wood
copper steel

questions.questionText: What is the unit of electromotive force (e.m.f.)?

options.text: ampere
newton
ohm
volt

questions.questionText:
Circuit breakers and fuses are devices used to protect a circuit from overloading.
Which statement correctly describes the difference between a circuit breaker and a fuse?

options.text: Circuit breakers can be reset if they operate but fuses need to be replaced.
Circuit breakers need to be replaced if they operate but fuses can be reset.
Circuit breakers can be used in an a.c. circuit but fuses cannot.
Circuit breakers cannot be used in an a.c. circuit but fuses can.

questions.questionText: Why might it be dangerous to use an electrical appliance in damp conditions?

options.text: It might lead to the fuse blowing.
It might lead to the insulation on the supply cable becoming damaged.
It might lead to an electric shock.
It might lead to the supply cable overheating.

questions.questionText:
A very important experiment improved scientists’ understanding of the structure of matter.
The experiment involved -particles being fired at a thin, gold foil.
What happened?

options.text: All the -particles were absorbed by the nuclei of the gold atoms.
All the -particles were unaffected by the gold atoms.
Some of the -particles were attracted by the neutrons in the nuclei of the gold atoms.
Some of the -particles were repelled by the protons in the nuclei of the gold atoms.

questions.questionText:
A nuclide has the symbol 23Na.
Which statement about all atoms of this nuclide is correct?

options.text: There are 11 protons in the nucleus.
There are 23 neutrons in the nucleus.
There are 11 electrons in the nucleus.
There are 34 nucleons in the nucleus.

questions.questionText: The half-life for lead-202 is 52500 years.

options.text: 105000 years
157500 years
210000 years
420000 years

questions.questionText: Why is a thick shield made of lead needed to protect people from a source of -rays?

options.text: Gamma radiation is strongly ionising and so is not very penetrating.
Gamma radiation is strongly ionising and so is very penetrating.
Gamma radiation is weakly ionising and so is not very penetrating.

Gamma radiation is weakly ionising and so is very penetrating.
